The routing of the Hutchinson probe through the Civil Rights Division is the tell. A lying-to-Congress allegation goes through the Criminal Division. Routing it through the Civil Rights Division - the specialized unit that handles police misconduct and systemic racial discrimination - bypasses the normal prosecutorial gatekeepers who would evaluate whether a viable case exists. The NYT reports that even within DOJ, officials have questioned from the start whether there’s a workable criminal case. The probe was opened anyway, while Bondi was fighting for her job. This is the same pattern that’s been documented across this administration’s retribution efforts. James Comey indicted. Letitia James indicted. John Brennan under stepped-up investigation. Adam Schiff under investigation. None of those cases have succeeded cleanly - courts have blocked them, grand juries have refused indictments, procedural mistakes have derailed prosecutions. But every one of them sent a signal to anyone currently inside the government watching what’s happening. Todd Blanche is now acting AG. His first public statement said DOJ is not focused on Trump’s enemies. He made that statement while NBC confirmed the department is also weighing the Hutchinson investigation going forward under his tenure. The investigation doesn’t have to produce a conviction to accomplish its purpose. Anyone sitting inside any administration, in any agency, watching what happens to people who testified truthfully about what they witnessed already understands what the stakes are. The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor in Kalpakkam attained criticality on Monday & is now only a step away from being fully operational. #CutTheClutter, with my colleague Soumya Pillai, explains why this is a key milestone, India’s 3-stage nuclear programme & its journey in this sector. 2. India’s 3-stage nuclear programme was conceived in the 1950s by Homi J Bhabha. Criticality is the second stage. This means a nuclear reactor can sustain a controlled chain reaction of fission, producing a constant power output. The PFBR is India’s first indigenously developed 500 MWe fast-breeder nuclear reactor. 3. The tech used in fast-breeder reactor differs from that in traditional nuclear reactors. Conventional nuclear reactors primarily use uranium as fuel, while fast breeder reactors use plutonium. India’s PFBR also uses plutonium as fuel, but it has been designed to eventually be able to use thorium, a radioactive element that is abundantly available in India. 4. An important thing to understand is that the tech is novel & very challenging. In Stage 2, for example, sodium is used as a coolant, which is extremely volatile. Many countries that started experimenting with this tech (Japan, France, South Korea, US etc) abandoned the programme. India persisted, partly because it had to. 5. India’s compulsion comes from 2 factors. First, India hardly has any uranium. It mines about 500 tons in a year, if at all. That’s out of a total global output of about 60,000 tons. So, India has to depend on imports & also those will have to be safeguarded. Second, of course, India has vast supply of thorium, about 25% of all the thorium in the world. 6. So, how exactly do the 3 stages work, why does it decades, and how will it help make India energy independent? Ahead of the Islamabad Talks A. Negotiations will be difficult. However, it’s important to recognize that this time the administration is bringing in Vice President Vance, who has a clear political interest in preventing a renewed escalation. Beyond domestic politics, Washington is acutely aware of the consequences of a breakdown: a major shock to global energy markets and highly problematic military options, ranging from strikes on civilian infrastructure to the risks of ground operations. In other words, both political incentives and strategic risks are pushing the U.S. toward avoiding collapse of the talks. B. The gaps between the parties remain significant. Iran’s leadership is unlikely to concede on its missile program, and certainly not on its right to enrich uranium. In any scenario involving full sanctions relief, the issue of the 60% 440 kg enriched uranium stockpile will likely become a central sticking point. C. The Strait of Hormuz issue is largely behind us. By effectively acknowledging Iran’s control over the strait, the U.S. has helped solidify this reality. Iran can already begin to reap the associated economic benefits. However, any expectation in Washington that Tehran will make concessions on force buildup or strategic capabilities is likely misplaced. D. While the current ceasefire is temporary, the costs of the war and, critically, the growing recognition in Washington that regime change is not achievable and that enriched uranium cannot be eliminated through military means, may soften the U.S. negotiating position. Unlike previous rounds (e.g., Geneva), the administration’s ability to credibly threaten war has diminished. From Tehran’s perspective, they have already endured the worst. E. Iran’s economic situation is dire, worse than before the war. Economic relief is therefore a critical priority for Tehran. That said, it is doubtful that Iran would trade core regime pillars for economic concessions F. One of Iran’s most significant achievements, especially given that it stepped back from insisting on a permanent ceasefire (assuming there are no undisclosed understandings about extending the truce or U.S. recognition of its right to enrich), is the apparent U.S. willingness to engage in negotiations based on Iran’s 10-point framework. G. This is notable because the gap between Iran’s 10 points and the administration’s 15-point framework remains substantial. The central question is whether Washington is prepared to move closer to Tehran’s positions, particularly on uranium enrichment and missile capabilities. These issues will be decisive not only for the negotiations, but for whether the conflict resumes. H. Who Really Wants the Deal? It is important to recognize that the push for negotiations originated in Washington. In practice, it was the Trump administration that shaped, if not dictated, the proposal conveyed via Pakistan for a two-week ceasefire. This matters because it suggests that the administration is entering the talks with a strong desire to reach an agreement quickly. I. That does not mean Iran lacks interest, far from it, given its economic situation, but the sense of urgency appears to be more pronounced on the U.S. side The bottom line is that current negotiations are not driven by optimism, but by a shared interest in avoiding further losses rather than securing victory. #IranWar‌

Prof. Ramesh Chand, Member, NITI Aayog, delivered the keynote address as Chief Guest at the policy dialogue on “Evidence-Led Food Systems Transformation Policies in the Context of Viksit Bharat,” organised by the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), ICAR and the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT). He highlighted the need to adopt a food systems approach in policy and practice, while underlining the associated challenges. He cautioned against the tendency to overlook evidence in designing incentives such as subsidies and support measures. He called upon agricultural economists to undertake rigorous benefit-cost analysis of policies, including populist measures, and to regularly publish such work to help build an enabling environment for evidence-based policymaking. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #ViksitBharat #AgriculturalEconomics #PolicyReform #SustainableAgriculture

Prof. Ramesh Chand, Member, NITI Aayog, delivered the keynote address at the high-level colloquium held at Centre for Research in Rural and Industrial Development (CRRID), where policymakers, economists and sector experts called for a calibrated shift towards diversification, sustainability and higher farmer incomes. He underlined that agricultural transformation must be guided by three core principles—growth, sustainability and remunerative employment. He emphasized that diversification cannot be seen as a “silver bullet” and must be pursued alongside improvements in existing cropping systems such as rice, wheat, cotton and mustard. He stated that providing input subsidies through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) is a more effective approach than financial packages to raise incomes of alternate crops to match paddy. He also highlighted that maize, supported by high-yielding varieties, can compete with rice if drainage systems are restored in Punjab. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #Agriculture #CropDiversification #FarmerIncomes #Sustainability

Assented to the Supplementary Appropriations Bill, 2026, at State House Nairobi. The Bill, now an Act, increases total expenditure by KSh393 billion from KSh4.3 trillion to KSh4.69 trillion. It aligns the national budget to address urgent and emerging priorities, including critical security operations, disaster response, and strategic infrastructure investments. The biggest share, KSh60 billion, was allocated to security, including KSh2 billion for the compensation of victims of protests. The education sector received KSh45.28 billion, reflecting the government’s commitment to deepen reform and the policy of universal schooling. The Affordable Housing Programme has been allocated KSh25 billion and agriculture close to KSh18 billion, KSh10 billion of which is for the subsidised fertiliser programme. On health, we have allocated KSh4 billion to clear pending bills under the defunct National Health Insurance Fund, KSh5.4 billion for the doctors internship programme, KSh2.5 billion for Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital and KSh2.6 billion for the vaccines programme. Additionally, KSh675 million has been set aside for the upgrading of Level 4 hospitals across the country. On its part, the Blue Economy and Fisheries Department has been allocated KSh350 million to organise the Oceanic Conference in Mombasa and Kilifi in June 2026, a meeting that will boost Kenya’s role in marine conservation and promote sustainable fisheries.

H.E. Elisa Maria da Silva today presented her Letter of Credence to the Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, at the ASEAN Headquarters/ASEAN Secretariat, formally commencing her tenure as the Permanent Representative of the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste to ASEAN. The Presentation of the Letter of Credence was followed by a courtesy call, during which Secretary-General Dr. Kao congratulated Ambassador Da Silva on her appointment and expressed confidence in her ability to contribute meaningfully to the ASEAN Community-building and regional integration efforts. ✍️ Les analystes convergent globalement vers une même lecture : la technologie évoquée repose sur une base scientifique réelle (magnétométrie quantique), mais son usage tel que décrit relève d’une extrapolation très agressive. Des experts en capteurs quantiques et en physique soulignent que la détection de signaux biologiques comme un battement de cœur est aujourd’hui limitée à des distances très courtes et dans des environnements contrôlés, et que le passage à une détection à grande distance dans un environnement ouvert est considéré comme non démontré, voire irréaliste avec les capacités actuelles. Côté analystes militaires, la lecture est encore plus claire : ils estiment que ce type de narration correspond à un schéma classique où une capacité expérimentale est “surinterprétée” dans la communication publique, soit pour masquer les véritables moyens utilisés (ISR, balises, thermique), soit pour projeter une image de supériorité technologique. En résumé, le consensus n’est pas de dire que “c’est faux”, mais que ce qui est décrit dépasse largement ce que la technologie permet aujourd’hui, et relève davantage d’un récit amplifié que d’une capacité opérationnelle crédible. Arab Intelligence - المخابرات العربية (@Arab_Intel) 🇺🇸🇮🇷 | Selon le New York Times, la CIA a utilisé une nouvelle technologie appelée « Ghost Murmur » pour localiser et aider au sauvetage du second aviateur lors du crash d’un F-15E. Cette technologie permettrait d’utiliser une « magnétométrie quantique à longue portée » afin de détecter l’empreinte électromagnétique d’un battement de cœur humain, puis d’associer ces données à un logiciel d’intelligence artificielle pour isoler ce signal du bruit environnant. « C’est comme entendre une voix dans un stade, sauf que le stade fait mille miles carrés de désert. Assented to the Supplementary Appropriations Bill, 2026, at State House Nairobi. The Bill, now an Act, increases total expenditure by KSh393 billion from KSh4.3 trillion to KSh4.69 trillion. It aligns the national budget to address urgent and emerging priorities, including critical security operations, disaster response, and strategic infrastructure investments. The biggest share, KSh60 billion, was allocated to security, including KSh2 billion for the compensation of victims of protests. The education sector received KSh45.28 billion, reflecting the government’s commitment to deepen reform and the policy of universal schooling. The Affordable Housing Programme has been allocated KSh25 billion and agriculture close to KSh18 billion, KSh10 billion of which is for the subsidised fertiliser programme. On health, we have allocated KSh4 billion to clear pending bills under the defunct National Health Insurance Fund, KSh5.4 billion for the doctors internship programme, KSh2.5 billion for Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital and KSh2.6 billion for the vaccines programme. Additionally, KSh675 million has been set aside for the upgrading of Level 4 hospitals across the country. On its part, the Blue Economy and Fisheries Department has been allocated KSh350 million to organise the Oceanic Conference in Mombasa and Kilifi in June 2026, a meeting that will boost Kenya’s role in marine conservation and promote sustainable fisheries.

Assented to the Supplementary Appropriations Bill, 2026, at State House Nairobi. The Bill, now an Act, increases total expenditure by KSh393 billion from KSh4.3 trillion to KSh4.69 trillion. It aligns the national budget to address urgent and emerging priorities, including critical security operations, disaster response, and strategic infrastructure investments. The biggest share, KSh60 billion, was allocated to security, including KSh2 billion for the compensation of victims of protests. The education sector received KSh45.28 billion, reflecting the government’s commitment to deepen reform and the policy of universal schooling. The Affordable Housing Programme has been allocated KSh25 billion and agriculture close to KSh18 billion, KSh10 billion of which is for the subsidised fertiliser programme. On health, we have allocated KSh4 billion to clear pending bills under the defunct National Health Insurance Fund, KSh5.4 billion for the doctors internship programme, KSh2.5 for Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital and KSh2.6 billion for the vaccines programme. Additionally, KSh675 million has been set aside for the upgrading of Level 4 hospitals across the country. On its part, the Blue Economy and Fisheries Department has been allocated KSh350 million to organise the Oceanic Conference in Mombasa and Kilifi in June 2026, a meeting that will boost Kenya’s role in marine conservation and promote sustainable fisheries.

Based on its independent analysis of new satellite imagery and detailed knowledge of the site, the IAEA can confirm recent impacts of military strikes close to Iran’s Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (BNPP), including one just 75 metres from the site perimeter. The BNPP itself has not been damaged, the IAEA’s analysis of the 5 April imagery shows. Once again, IAEA Director General @rafaelmgrossi warns that continued military activity near the BNPP - an operating plant with large amounts of nuclear fuel - could cause a severe radiological accident with harmful consequences for people and the environment in Iran and beyond. Regardless of the nature of the intended targets, DG Grossi says such attacks pose a very real danger to nuclear safety and must stop. DG Grossi reiterates call for all parties to fully respect the 7 indispensable pillars for ensuring nuclear safety and security during a conflict. A nuclear facility and surrounding areas should never be struck, DG Grossi says.

The IAEA has been informed by Iran that a projectile struck close to the premises of the Bushehr NPP this morning, the fourth such incident in recent weeks. Iran also informed the IAEA that one of the site’s physical protection staff members was killed by a projectile fragment and that a building on site was affected by shockwaves and fragments. No increase in radiation levels was reported. IAEA DG @rafaelmgrossi expresses deep concern about the reported incident and says NPP sites or nearby areas must never be attacked, noting that auxiliary site buildings may contain vital safety equipment. Reiterating call for maximum military restraint to avoid risk of a nuclear accident, DG Grossi again stresses the paramount importance of adhering to the 7 pillars for ensuring nuclear safety and security during a conflict.

The miniature figures below are yong – funerary objects made of pottery or wood, often fashioned in the form of humans or animals and intended to serve the tomb occupant in the afterlife. The most famous examples of these substitute attendants are the life-sized warriors of the Terracotta Army buried with China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang. Domestic servants, including musicians and dancers like those shown here, also constituted a large share of such figurines. Unearthed from a Han-dynasty (206 BC-220 AD) tomb, these figures offer historians a rare glimpse into the lives of aristocratic families more than 2,000 years ago. समता आणि सामाजिक न्यायासाठी आजीवन समर्पित राहिलेल्या महात्मा जोतिबा फुले यांच्या 200 व्या जयंतीच्या उपलक्ष्यात संस्कृती मंत्रालय दोन वर्षे (2026 ते 2028) चालणाऱ्या राष्ट्रव्यापी समारंभाचा शुभारंभ करणार आहे. वंचित वर्गांच्या उत्थानासाठी आणि कल्याणासाठी जोतिबा फुले यांनी शिक्षणाला हत्यार बनवले. त्यांनी केवळ देशातील पहिले बालिका विद्यालय स्थापन केले नाही, तर सत्यशोधक समाजाची स्थापना करून सामाजिक समतेबद्दल लोकांमध्ये जागृती निर्माण केली. त्यांचे जीवन आजही देशासाठी प्रेरणेचा स्रोत आहे. त्यांच्या 200 व्या जयंतीनिमित्त आयोजित दोन वर्षीय कार्यक्रमांचा उद्देश्य तरुणांना जोतिबा फुले यांच्या विचारांशी जोडत सर्वसमावेशक समाजाच्या निर्मितीसाठी प्रेरित करणे हा आहे. #JyotibaPhule200 #CultureUnitesAll

समानता और सामाजिक न्याय के लिये आजीवन समर्पित रहे महात्मा ज्योतिबा फुले जी की 200वीं जयंती के उपलक्ष्य में संस्कृति मंत्रालय दो वर्ष (2026 से 2028) तक चलने वाले राष्ट्रव्यापी समारोह का शुभारंभ करने जा रहा है। वंचित वर्गों के उत्थान और कल्याण के लिये ज्योतिबा फुले जी ने शिक्षा को हथियार बनाया, उन्होंने ना सिर्फ देश में पहला बालिका विद्यालय स्थापित किया बल्कि सत्यशोधक समाज की स्थापना कर सामाजिक समानता के प्रति लोगों को जागरुक किया। उनका जीवन आज भी देश के लिये एक प्रेरणा का स्रोत है। उनकी 200वीं जयंती पर चलने वाले दो वर्षीय कार्यक्रमों का उद्देश्य युवाओं को ज्योतिबा फुले जी के विचारों से जोड़ते हुए उन्हें समावेशी समाज के निर्माण के लिये प्रेरित करना है। #JyotibaPhule200 #CultureUnitesAll

A session on “ Data Insights for Citizen Centricity: A Grassroots Perspective” was organised by the Capacity Building Commission as part of Sādhana Saptah. Shri Rohit Kumar, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, Aspirational Districts & Blocks Programme (ADP/ABP), NITI Aayog, shared insights from the implementation of the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) and Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP). He highlighted how real-time data, continuous monitoring, and evidence-based Governance is helping strengthen last-mile delivery and improve development outcomes in aspirational geographies. The session also emphasised the importance of connecting grassroots-level insights with institutional decision-making to enable more responsive and citizen-centric governance. The discussion offered valuable reflections on building systems that are adaptive, outcome-oriented, and rooted in the lived realities of people. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #AspirationalDistricts #AspirationalBlocks #DataDrivenGovernance #GoodGovernance #CitizenCentricity #LastMileDelivery

NITI Aayog convened a National Level Consultative Meeting on “Institutional Structures & Processes for Research Translation and Productisation” on 6th April, 2026 at NITI Aayog, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Dr V. K. Saraswat, Member (S&T). The meeting brought together Directors and CEOs of leading Research Parks, Innovation Hubs, and S&T Clusters to deliberate on institutional models and processes for research translation and productisation. In his opening remarks, Dr Saraswat highlighted the gap between industry and academia, emphasizing the need for enablers to strengthen collaboration. He noted continued reliance on imported technologies and called for robust frameworks and measurable metrics to scale research translation across the country. Discussions focused on strengthening institutional mechanisms, including testing and prototyping facilities, Technology Transfer Offices (TTOs), industry-focused PhD programmes, and funding support through RDIF for startups and MSMEs. NITI Aayog reaffirmed its commitment to fostering coordinated efforts across institutions, industry, and government to drive research translation and technology development. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #Innovation #ResearchTranslation #TechnologyDevelopment #AtmanirbharBharat

#hackerthrowback For the young hackers who don't know all the history yet, and since we've been talking about some of this recently: Here is a list of all the papers / talks I can remember giving: 2004 Reverse Engineering Malcious Binaries - focusing on unix malware and RE approaches. - redcrowlab.com/papers/061820… 2004 Discovering and Exploiting HTTP Vulnerabilities - Early example of MiTM attacks against a CUPS print server web application. - redcrowlab.com/papers/070820… 2004 Advanced Firewall Penetration Methos (with Delchi) - Approaches for bypassing firewalls, session hijacking, reverse shells, VPN piggybacking, tunneling to bypass egress filtering. - redcrowlab.com/papers/120520… 2005 Finding and Exploiting Simple Local Buffer Overflows - Talks through intel CPU architecture, finding vulnerable target binaries, early fuzzing, dynamic instrumentation to analyze memory, shell code development, and exploitation. redcrowlab.com/papers/051520… 2006 Defcon - Hacking Malware - Virtual machine detection, ways of bypassing malware obfuscation, trampoline exploits against malware (like Sasser) and the release of Offensive Computing (an automated malware analysis and community site similar to Virustotal before Virustotal existed.) media.defcon.org/DEF%20CON%2… Also the exploit / metasploit module : redcrowlab.com/papers/112620… 2006 Detecting the Presence of Virtual Machines Using the Local Data Table (with Quist) - Virtual machine detection was important in advanced malware armoring. This paper gives a new approach. redcrowlab.com/papers/032220… 2006 Defcon Further Down the VM Spiral (with Quist) - More advanced approaches to virtual machine detection. redcrowlab.com/papers/080420… 2006 Around this time Quist and I gave a lecture at The Santa Fe Institute on automated malware analysis. I can't find any records about it as it was a private small Summit event with major CTOs and execs (Microsoft, CISCO, etc.) 2007 Blackhat and Defcon - Covert Debugging Circumventing Software Armoring (with Quist) - Techniques for automated unpacking / deobfuscating of malware - blackhat.com/presentations/b… redcrowlab.com/papers/080320… youtube.com/watch?v=IeMCCZD5… 2007 Defcon Malware Secrets (with delchi) approaches to gathering threat and brand intelligence from a huge malware collection. Release of PIZDA tool. AV comparatives. - redcrowlab.com/papers/050820… youtube.com/watch?v=E73leOVW… 2007 Blackhat and Defcon - Tactial Exploitation (with HDM) - A ton of hacker techniques for breaking into systems including ssh hijacking, kerberos ticket stealing, all kinds of enumeration, war dialing. This talk became a training class for many years. We had like 5000 people in the audience, the fire marshal came. - blackhat.com/presentations/b… blackhat.com/presentations/b… m.youtube.com/watch?v=_Webzm… Around this time I gave a guest lecture at New Mexico Tech on memory corruption exploitation. 2008 ShmooCon – Malware Software Armoring Circumvention (also referred to as Covert Debugging: Circumventing Software Armoring Techniques) (with Danny Quist) - This was the follow-up/expanded version of the 2007 Black Hat/DEF CON covert debugging talk. It covered the Saffron covert debugging platform using dynamic instrumentation and page-fault assisted debugging to unpack/obfuscated malware without triggering anti-analysis tricks. Defcon 2008 Meta-Post Exploitation - Post-exploitation techniques including how to manage 1000s of passwords, cracking sessions, spraying, stealthy supply chain attack examples, and released the tools MetaPass, MassNetUse, MassWinEnum, AtAbuse - defcon.org/images/defcon-16/… youtube.com/watch?v=swCNI1qW… Blackhat DC 2009 - Dissecting Web Attacks / Blog Spam (With Colin Ames) - We completely tore apart a huge malware compaign using web site injection and even achieved some level of attribution. blackhat.com/presentations/b… blackhat.com/presentations/b… 2009 Sky Talks - The Internet - Gave a more conceptual talk on security in general. redcrowlab.com/papers/071120… 2009 Blackhat and Defcon (with Ames and Kerb) MetaPhish - We released a PDF infector (later used by malware gangs) a C2 over Tor, a Self Signed Java Applet Attack, and web techniques for managing phishing campaigns. redcrowlab.com/papers/080520… redcrowlab.com/papers/080520… I also gave this same talk at a SANS summit I think that same year. This was part of the Metasploit Track I ran at Blackhat as well. 2009 First Ever Bsides - Forgotten talk, but I was one of the first speakers there. No video exists as far as I know. 2009 phpBB Exploit Released - Arbitrary Code Execution and Metasploit Module - exploit-db.com/exploits/1689… 2010 Samba 2.2.8 Solaris SPARC trans2open RCE Metasploit Module CVE 2003-0201 - exploit-db.com/exploits/1633… 2010 I think Blackhat DC (with Potter) - Why Blackhats Always Win - Things blackhat hackers have to worry about and the major differences between penetration testers and blackhat hackers. I gave a talk at toorcon in the 2000s but I don't remember exactly when or what the topic was but it might have been this as well. If anyone remembers it let me know. blackhat.com/presentations/b… redcrowlab.com/papers/010820… 2010 Blackhat and Defcon (With Ames and Lai) - Balancing the Pwn Trade Deficit - Deep dive into Chinese hacking groups and techniques as well as malware RE - media.blackhat.com/bh-us-10/… youtube.com/watch?v=vZPdcf_F… 2011 Blackhat DC (with Polyokov) - Forgotten World Hacking ERP - We hacked a ton of ERP systems including Oracle, Russian ones, JD Edwards, and dropped 0day. - redcrowlab.com/papers/011820… redcrowlab.com/papers/021820… 2011 - 2015 - Sometime during these years I gave a couple of guest lectures at UNM on cyber security. I gave several talks at Boston Source, Source Europe, and Blackhat Europe all repeats of previous talks. Gave a talk at FBI Infragard (following Frank Abignale) - No slides or video exists. I also gave a Malware Analysis talk at the Pentagon - No slides or video exists. 2011 - BSIdes Las Vegas - Are There Still Wolves Among Us - An Anti-sec style talk tearing the security community a new one. No published slides or video exists. I retired from speaking for several years at this point, although I continued giving training classes at Blackhat on Tactical Exploitation and Tactical Response (IR) until maybe around 2015. I also gave a bunch of training classes to the gov, mil, Cylance, and other places. 2017 OWASP San Diego - I came out of retirement briefly to give a talk "What I've Learned" covering a lot of cyber war stories and things I'd been through. redcrowlab.com/papers/092120… 2024 BSides Albuquerque - Industrial Scale Hardware Hacking - Details my process for mass hacking IoT, OT, and other hardware devices including firmware dumping and reversing, RF domain analysis, network and web attacks, logic and scope analysis, etc. redcrowlab.com/papers/071920… There are a ton of citations in other people's papers and talks as well as a couple books like Gray Hat Hacking: The Ethical Hacker’s Handbook

Shri Rohit Kumar, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, Aspirational Districts & Blocks Programme (ADP/ABP), NITI Aayog, delivered a presentation on “Aspirational District Programme / Aspirational Block Programme: Contours, Challenges and Way Forward” at the National Defence College, New Delhi. The session provided an opportunity to reflect on how the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) and Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP) have emerged as important instruments for strengthening governance, improving service delivery, and accelerating development outcomes in geographically underserved areas. The presentation highlighted the key contours of ADP and ABP, emphasising convergence, collaboration, competition, and evidence-based monitoring. It also underlined how focused attention to districts and blocks can support responsive administration, improve implementation across critical sectors, and strengthen last-mile delivery through continuous review and coordinated action. The discussion further examined the challenges ahead, including the need to deepen institutional capacity, sustain momentum at the field level, improve inter-departmental coordination, and ensure that development gains translate into long-term structural transformation. It also outlined the way forward for making aspirational geographies stronger engines of inclusive growth through sharper implementation, stronger partnerships, and continued focus on measurable outcomes. The interactive exchange with course participants enriched the session and reflected the importance of governance innovations that can deliver impact at scale. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #AspirationalDistricts #AspirationalBlocks #InclusiveDevelopment #GoodGovernance #LastMileDelivery #ViksitBharat

#DidYouKnow The SWAR (System of Water for Agriculture Rejuvenation) initiative in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh demonstrated how innovative irrigation can improve water efficiency in drought-prone regions. The system shifted irrigation to the plant root zone using buried clay pots and micro-tubes, enabling precise and sustained moisture delivery based on crop needs. Compared to drip irrigation, SWAR used one-third of the water with minimal wastage, and in some crops like vegetables and fruits, as little as one-eighth of the water was sufficient. The intervention also improved soil health, crop productivity, and farmers’ incomes. These achievements have been documented as Best Practices on the NITI for States (NFS) Knowledge Portal -an initiative under the State Support Mission. Navigation satellites are invisible infrastructure - until they aren't. In an era where GPS signals are being jammed over conflict zones, spoofed to sink ships, and denied to adversaries in wartime, controlling your own navigation system has become a marker of true strategic sovereignty. India built NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) for exactly this reason. But today, the system is barely functional - crippled by atomic clock failures, delayed launches, and years of institutional neglect. In this episode, we examine what NavIC's crisis reveals about India's space priorities, what it costs the military, and what it would actually take to fix it. Join Ashwin Prasad (@ashwinpras), Hitesh Gala and Arindam Goswami (@AriGos) in this episode of All Things Policy where we discuss all this and more. Marc Andreessen thinks Elon Musk hasn't just built successful companies, he might have actually cracked the code on how to manage for the next hundred years. The fundamental problem with any traditional organization that has multiple layers of management is what Andreessen brilliantly describes as "compounding lies." Every layer distorts reality just a little bit more until the original mission is completely lost in the bureaucracy. Musk’s method completely destroys that outdated corporate structure. It relies entirely on an extreme focus on substance and getting straight to the truth. By stripping away the noise, he has figured out the exact blueprint to reconcile being a chaotic fountain of ideas with being a ruthless, systematic builder. Video

In an era where GPS signals are being jammed over conflict zones, spoofed to sink ships, and denied to adversaries in wartime, controlling your own navigation system has become a marker of true strategic sovereignty. India built NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) for exactly this reason. But today, the system is barely functional - crippled by atomic clock failures, delayed launches, and years of institutional neglect. But today, the system has run into operational issues due to atomic clock failures and launch delays. Last week of March, against the rocky slopes of Nandi Hills, under a relentless sun, 24 participants across four squads took on one big policy question. How do we build stronger capacity for vaccine R&D in India? India manufactures vaccines for the world. But cutting-edge vaccine discovery still lags behind. At stake is not just innovation, but India’s health security, economic opportunity, and position in a rapidly evolving global biotech landscape. The challenge isn’t production. It’s strengthening our capacity for vaccine discovery. Over many rounds of discussion, our four squads, Bade Log, X-rna, Artha, and Dravya, stepped into the shoes of policymakers, researchers, and industry leaders. They worked through trade-offs, designed incentives, questioned assumptions, and developed pathways to strengthen India’s vaccine innovation ecosystem. These photos capture a moment just after their presentations, a mix of relief, pride, and hard-earned clarity. #11YearsOfMUDRA में मोदी सरकार ने छोटे व्यापारियों और स्टार्टअप्स को बिना गारंटी के ऋण उपलब्ध कराकर स्वरोजगार और लघु उद्योग को नई शक्ति दी है। इन 11 वर्षों में इस कल्याणकारी योजना के तहत ₹40 लाख करोड़ से अधिक के 58 करोड़ लोन वितरित किए जा चुके हैं, जिससे 12 करोड़ युवा लाभान्वित होकर आत्मनिर्भर भारत की निर्माण यात्रा को नई ऊर्जा दे रहे हैं। हर 3 में से 2 मुद्रा ऋण महिलाओं को मिलना नारी शक्ति के स्वावलंबन की दिशा में ऐतिहासिक उपलब्धि है।

1857 की क्रांति को अपने अदम्य शौर्य से नई ऊर्जा देने वाले मंगल पांडे जी ने एक तरफ युवाओं को माँ भारती की स्वाधीनता के लिए प्रेरित किया, वहीं अपनी संस्कृति से किसी भी सूरत में समझौता नहीं किया। उनके नेतृत्व में बैरकपुर छावनी अंग्रेजी हुकूमत के खिलाफ संघर्ष की प्रतीक बन गई। मातृभूमि के प्रति उनकी अटूट निष्ठा, साहस और बलिदान गाथा आज भी रोम-रोम में राष्ट्रप्रेम की भावना को और भी मजबूत बनाती है। महान स्वतंत्रता सेनानी मंगल पांडे जी को उनके बलिदान दिवस पर नमन करता हूँ।

अपनी लेखनी से पूरे भारत में राष्ट्रभक्ति की अलख जगाने वाले और मातृभूमि के लिए संघर्ष करने का मंत्र देने वाले बंकिम चंद्र चट्टोपाध्याय जी को उनकी पुण्यतिथि पर कोटि-कोटि नमन। बंकिम बाबू ने भारत के लोगों को संघर्ष करने की ऊर्जा और साहस दिया। उन्होंने ऐसे समय में भारतीय समाज के आत्मसम्मान को जागृत करने का कार्य किया, जब देश अंग्रेजी शासन के अन्याय और शोषण से पीड़ित था। उनकी लेखनी केवल साहित्य नहीं, बल्कि स्वतंत्रता की चेतना और राष्ट्रीय स्वाभिमान का प्रखर उद्घोष थी। ‘वन्दे मातरम्’ के माध्यम से उन्होंने स्वतंत्रता संग्राम को एक ऐसा मंत्र दिया, जिसने पूरे राष्ट्र को एकता के सूत्र में पिरो दिया। बंकिम बाबू ने अपने लेखन से भारत के लोगों को यह स्मरण कराया कि भारत एक महान सभ्यता और संस्कृति है। ऐसे युगदृष्टा के प्रति यह राष्ट्र सदैव कृतज्ञ रहेगा।

भारत के प्रथम स्वाधीनता संग्राम में बैरकपुर छावनी से क्रांति का बिगुल फूंकने वाले अमर सेनानी मंगल पांडे जी के बलिदान दिवस पर मैं उन्हें नमन करता हूँ। उनका बलिदान मातृभूमि और भारतीय संस्कृति की रक्षा के लिए, हर तरह का त्याग करने की हम सबको प्रेरणा देता है। यह देश उनके बलिदान को हमेशा याद रखेगा।

"Only because they have a warrant." Alright, some Law 101. Warrants are not optional. Law enforcement *cannot* decline to execute a warrant. A warrant isn't only a Court order granting permission to do something; it is a Court order *commanding* you to do it. Application for a warrant is (sometimes) optional. Execution of it once granted, or issued sua sponte by the Judge, is non-negotiable. When I was a prosecutor, I would periodically receive calls from LEOs asking me to help them get out of executing a warrant—either because the situation looked bad, the specific situation was disproportionate in their eyes, or in one instance because the defendant was in a coma. Every time my answer was the same: Its a Court order. We cannot disobey it. If I tell them to disobey it, I can suffer disciplinary action up to and including jail time for contempt or losing my law license (unlikely unless its a repeat problem, to be candid). We can file motions to ask the Court to quash a warrant, but that is up to the Court. Until so quashed, if an LEO *can* execute the warrant, they *must* execute the warrant. LEOs and Prosecutors do have a lot of discretion, but not nearly as much as some people seem to believe. Jeremy Shreffler (@Jshreffler1977) It’s a perfect defense for cops in America today. If social media posts of Judge Hamayoun Dilawar are authentic (Tosha Khana Case Judge), this is alarming and raises serious and reasonable doubts on credibility of trial being conducted by him. In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

HOW THE WAR HAS ENDED FOR IRAN 🚨 1. Regime still calling the shots. Iran’s leadership structure remains intact. No regime collapse, no internal overthrow, and Tehran continues to dictate its own political and military posture. 2. Hormuz still Iran’s lever. The Strait of Hormuz remains under Iran’s shadow. Despite weeks of conflict, the war has not removed Tehran’s ability to threaten or influence the world’s most critical energy chokepoint. 3. Nuclear material still inside Iran. Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile has not been seized, destroyed or relocated. The core nuclear question that triggered global alarm remains unresolved. 4. Military capacity badly hit but not erased. Iran’s military structure has taken losses but remains functional. Missile forces, air defence networks and command structures continue to operate. 5. Long-range strike capability survives. Iran has demonstrated it can still launch long-range strikes across the Gulf region, hitting bases and infrastructure far beyond its borders. 6. Tehran showed no rush to end the war Iran has projected patience, showing little urgency to end hostilities while allowing the conflict to grind down its adversaries politically and militarily. 7. Washington appeared more eager for a ceasefire. As the conflict dragged on, the messaging increasingly suggested the United States wanted an off-ramp faster than Iran did. 8. US and Israel now visibly split on war aims. Differences between Washington and Tel Aviv over the objectives and acceptable end terms of the war have become more visible, something Iran has capitalised on. 9. US air defence reserves heavily drained. The scale of Iranian missile and drone attacks forced the United States to expend large numbers of interceptors in the Gulf, reportedly even pulling systems from Pacific allocations. 10.Major damage inflicted on US regional assets. Iran has managed to hit high-value military infrastructure and sensors across Gulf states, imposing tangible costs on the US military presence in the region.

A few hard truths about the emerging ceasefire: it may signal the beginning of the end of the fighting, but given the deep mistrust between the parties, it must be treated with extreme caution. Until a ceasefire is fully in place, there is no ceasefire: 1. We are still operating in the dark. Key details are missing, especially what was actually promised to Iran. 2. If Iran did in fact secure guarantees based on the ‘ten principles’ Trump referenced, that is not a marginal outcome, it is a strategic win for Tehran, reinforcing its narrative and positioning. 3. Iran will almost certainly frame this as a success: a temporary ceasefire backed by assurances on negotiations under its terms and constraints on renewed military action. Whether that perception reflects reality remains unclear, but perception matters. 4. Any assessment must start with a basic fact: Iran still holds enriched uranium. That reality has not changed. 5. The United States has chosen, at least for now, to avoid escalation and signal flexibility. But the practical meaning of this, especially regarding Iran’s economic lifelines remains vague. What is not vague is President Trump’s clear preference for reaching a deal, even with a regime he has aggressively targeted. 6. When forced to choose, Trump did not fully align with Israel’s position and instead moved toward a ceasefire. That decision carries implications but it is too early to determine how far they will go. 7. And if there was any doubt about Trump’s priorities, look at the Strait of Hormuz. Keeping it open, after it remained open even at the start of the war, clearly became the central objective of the negotiations, above all else. That alone says a lot. It underscores just how flawed the strategic planning of this campaign was from the outset. More to follow! I mostly avoid commenting on what President Trump says from day to day, while pulling no punches in my assessments, whether positive or negative, of his policy. His Iran ultimatums feel different. Making such threats is a policy. If he were to follow through on them, the consequences would be immediate, irreversible, and catastrophic on a world-historical scale. So while some will inevitably insist he should be “taken seriously rather than literally,” or that he is executing a sophisticated “madman” strategy in a complex game of 5-D chess, or that he needs everyone’s steadfast support to maximize his leverage, now rather than later seems the time to say that the actions that he is proposing would be a disaster for our country, both strategically and morally, which makes the remarks themselves a terrible mistake. Simply put, what’s the point of all this? If these are empty threats that we all know he will not carry out, then they are ineffective threats (the Iranians are on X too!), merely making the president and our nation look foolish. If they are not empty threats, then the president is asserting the American position that such actions are acceptable in this situation and ones we are willing to take. We are not living in some quantum thought experiment where he simultaneously is and is not serious. We cannot expect the Iranians, but only the Iranians, will believe him. Whether the threats are empty or not, we should be willing to say: This is wrong. We should not establish a pattern of threatening escalation from a blockaded strait to elimination of a civilization. We should not launch strikes intended to devastate the lives of millions of people and take our nation to total war without indisputable justification, or before the American people have deliberated upon and assented to the path with full understanding of what total war might mean for them. Those principles are vital to our Republic, independent of whether the strategy could “work.” But it’s also worth emphasizing that the strategy is a dead end. This war is actively weakening American power, increasing the danger to American citizens, and frustrating the president’s important efforts at addressing our many domestic challenges. It has closed a strait that was previously open, strengthened the incentive for other nations to pursue nuclear weapons, and in this most recent rhetoric made more plausible their use. Our choices for continuing the war appear to be catastrophic escalation of the air war or extensive deployment of ground troops, neither of which were planned or had support at the outset. Stepping back from these threats and admitting such actions do not offer a path to resolving the conflict may be unpalatable, but it is by far the least unpalatable option available. Let us all hope cooler heads prevail.

He also apprised the Crown Prince on latest developments in Pakistan’s mediation efforts to de-escalate the Middle East crisis. The Prime Minister conveyed his warm wishes and respectful regards for The Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, His Majesty King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. The Crown Prince appreciated Pakistan’s peace efforts, aimed at restoring peace and stability in the region.

बोरिवली भूयारी मार्ग प्रकल्पा'साठी 'टनेल बोरिंग मशीन - नायक'चा शुभारंभही करण्यात आला. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, मेट्रो मार्ग 9 च्या पहिल्या टप्प्यात दहिसर पूर्व, पांडुरंगवाडी, मीरागाव आणि काशीगाव अशी स्थानके असून, ही मेट्रो लाईन-7 शी जोडली गेल्याने प्रवाशांना अधिक चांगली कनेक्टिव्हिटी मिळणार आहे. दुसऱ्या टप्प्यात साईबाबा नगर ते सुभाषचंद्र बोस मैदान या मार्गाचे काम 96 टक्के पूर्ण झाले असून, याच वर्षात त्याचेही उदघाटन करण्याचा राज्य शासनाचा प्रयत्न आहे. सुमारे ₹6607 कोटी खर्चाच्या या प्रकल्पामुळे सध्या एक ते दोन तास लागणारा प्रवास केवळ 30 मिनिटांत पूर्ण होणार आहे. पुढील टप्प्यांमध्ये ही मेट्रो लाईन-3 शी जोडली जाणार असून, मीरा-भाईंदर ते कुलाबा दरम्यान अखंड प्रवासाची सुविधा उपलब्ध होणार आहे. मेट्रो मार्गिका 2 (ब) च्या पहिल्या टप्प्याचे लोकार्पण व पॉड टॅक्सी प्रकल्पाच्या भूमिपूजनप्रसंगी मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, या मार्गावरील पाच स्थानके आजपासून सुरू होत आहेत. या मार्गिकेचे उर्वरित दोन टप्पे पूर्ण झाल्यानंतर मुंबईत मोठ्या प्रमाणावर सुसंगत आणि जलद कनेक्टिव्हिटी उपलब्ध होईल. तसेच या प्रकल्पामुळे पूर्व-पश्चिम तसेच उत्तर-दक्षिण मुंबई एकमेकांशी प्रभावीपणे जोडली जाणार आहेत. भविष्यात बीकेसी, अंधेरी, वांद्रे आणि चेंबूरपर्यंत अखंड प्रवास सुलभ होणार. ही मेट्रो हार्बर लाईनला जोडणारी पहिली मेट्रो ठरत असल्याने वाहतूक व्यवस्थेत नवा अध्याय सुरू होणार आहे. तसेच पॉड टॅक्सी प्रकल्पामुळे बीकेसीमधील वाहतूक कोंडी कमी होण्यास मदत होईल. हा प्रकल्प बीओटी तत्त्वावर राबविण्यात येणार असून, 20 महिन्यांत पहिला टप्पा पूर्ण करण्याचे उद्दिष्ट ठेवण्यात आले आहे. Com adesão de todos os estados e 5.565 municípios (99%), saímos de um patamar de 36% das crianças alfabetizadas ao fim do 2º ano do Fundamental em 2021 para 66% em 2025. O Compromisso Nacional Criança Alfabetizada foi criado com essa intenção e para ajudar a recuperar a defasagem no aprendizado de crianças em função da pandemia de Covid-19. A iniciativa já teve investimentos superiores a R$ 1,5 bilhão, que incluem a implementação de 174.619 Cantinhos da Leitura e a capacitação de 643 mil professores e 7,2 mil articuladores nas cinco regiões. Como parte do esforço, o Governo do Brasil criou o Selo Nacional Compromisso com a Alfabetização, que premia redes de ensino que se empenham na formulação e implementação de políticas para garantir o direito à alfabetização das crianças até o fim do 2º ano do fundamental. Neste ano, 11 estados e 2.274 municípios foram reconhecidos com o selo ouro.
